evals.prompt: I'm inside Herdr. Implement the requested API change with a separate coding agent, keep the work isolated, then have another agent review the exact implementation commit before you call it done. Don't push or merge anything.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the delivery path; records the intake lane, scope, ownership, base, checks, plan, exclusions, and a partition (one scope unless the analysis shows disjoint owned paths); creates only the needed Engineer and Reviewer panes in the caller's existing checkout; names the Lead seat and ends its turn while Peers report back by prompt, reconciling herdr agent list once per wake; requires each Engineer's evidence report, then quiesces, stages by owned paths, commits, and runs the acceptance checks on that exact head itself; performs an independent no-mutation review on that exact head; routes any fix back to the owning Engineer; does not push or merge.
assertions: Selects the delivery route rather than the lightweight or review-only route
Records an intake result naming lane, reason, owners, plan, claim-shaped validation, and a partition with owned paths
Has the Lead commit the Engineers' work at a quiesce point and run the acceptance checks on that exact head before review, rather than accepting an agent's own commit or check results as evidence
Runs an independent no-mutation review bound to that exact head
Sends a charter whose ownership boundary is binding but whose solution shape stays provisional, without a predetermined implementation or disguised conclusion
Does not push or merge

evals.prompt: Use Herdr to review commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 in the current project. I only want an independent review of that head; do not create an Engineer and do not change files.
evals.expected_output: Uses the review-only path; verifies Herdr context and the named exact head; does not create an Engineer or extra Lead; instructs the Reviewer not to mutate; checks HEAD and porcelain before and after; checks lane/plan/validation consistency and relevant proof boundaries; returns PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with evidence bound to that SHA.
assertions: Uses the review-only route and creates no Engineer
Binds the verdict to the named exact SHA
Records HEAD and git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain --untracked-files=all before and after the review
Attempts to disconfirm the material claims with concrete failure scenarios instead of confirming the implementation narrative
Returns one of PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with file/line evidence

evals.prompt: I'm in Herdr. Split a sibling pane to the right in the same directory and run `pnpm test` there, leaving my current pane focused.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the lightweight route and handles it from the CLI reference alone; verifies HERDR_ENV, preserves the caller cwd and focus, splits one sibling pane with no focus, runs the command in that pane, and does not read the delivery policies or create an implementation/Reviewer pipeline, extra Lead, or recurring watch.
assertions: Chooses the lightweight route and reads only the CLI reference, not the delivery policies
Preserves the caller's focus and working directory
Creates no Reviewer, extra Lead, or recurring watch

evals.prompt: In Herdr, update the authentication storage format and add a dual-read fallback so old sessions keep working. It may require migration and changes to the public API. Have an agent implement it and another review it, but don't make any irreversible or external changes without my decision.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as high-risk; records the reason and affected security/data/public-contract boundaries; treats dual-read/fallback and migration as a design gate; records constraints, alternatives, failure modes, owner, validation, stop conditions, and the required Human decision in an active plan before implementation; does not silently implement the compatibility path or perform external/irreversible actions.
assertions: Classifies the work as high-risk and names the security, data, or public-contract impact
Treats the dual-read/fallback and migration request as a design gate needing an explicit decision
Records constraints, alternatives, failure modes, owner, validation, and stop conditions before implementation
Does not perform irreversible or external actions without the Human decision

evals.prompt: I'm in Herdr and a small adapter around the database keeps retrying, caching partial state, and translating errors because the database client doesn't expose the lifecycle information we need. Review whether this is a safe local fix or whether the owner module needs repair, and tell me what evidence would distinguish a justified deviation from a structural problem.
evals.expected_output: Reads the structural-misfit policy as conditional lenses; checks mechanism, ownership, lifecycle, information sufficiency, duplicate state, retry/failure semantics, and proof laundering; compares the local patch with an owner-clean route; reports evidence, concrete tax, and a disconfirming check, and either issues one of STANDARD_FIT, JUSTIFIED_DEVIATION, or STRUCTURAL_CONCERN on the evidence it has or pre-registers the rule that would decide it without treating the lenses as a mandatory checklist or manufacturing blockers.
assertions: Treats the structural-misfit lenses as conditional, not as a mandatory checklist
Compares the local patch against an owner-clean route
Reports evidence, a concrete tax, and a disconfirming check

Either returns STANDARD_FIT, JUSTIFIED_DEVIATION, or STRUCTURAL_CONCERN with the evidence behind it, or names the evidence that would decide between them and commits to the decision rule before collecting it

evals.prompt: I'm implementing a normal Herdr task on the delivery branch. The change unexpectedly touches authorization and could delete user data, even though the original request looked local and reversible. Continue only if the workflow remains safe.

assertions: Stops before crossing the original boundary
Raises the lane from normal to high-risk on the authorization and data-loss evidence
Emits REOPEN_REQUEST with old lane, proposed lane, boundary, and decision needed
Waits for the Lead or Human decision instead of continuing

Names a pre-chosen fallback kind pinned to the same exact head and states all four fallback triggers: unavailable kind, error or no verdict, only remaining kind being an Engineer kind, and a read-only or no-mutation violation

evals.prompt: In Herdr I've just sent charters to three Engineers, web-scope, api-scope, and docs-scope, for one partitioned issue. Wait for them and handle whatever comes back.
evals.expected_output: Does not run herdr agent wait, agent prompt --wait, a sleep loop, or repeated herdr agent list; explains that each Engineer reports by herdr agent prompt to the Lead seat and that each report wakes the Lead, and ends the turn with one printed line, Awaiting reports: web-scope, api-scope, docs-scope. On each wake handles the reporting Peer from its report, then before ending that turn runs herdr agent list once and reconciles: an idle or done Peer with no report is read from its pane, a blocked Peer is inspected with agent get and agent read and its approval dialog routed as a Human decision rather than answered by inference, a Peer missing from the list is restaffed; ends every such turn with an Awaiting reports line naming the Peers still owed; does not commit, review, or hand off while any Engineer's report is outstanding.
assertions: Ends the turn and relies on Peer reports arriving by prompt instead of any wait, sleep loop, or polling of herdr agent list
Ends each turn that still has reports outstanding with a printed Awaiting reports line naming those Peers
Handles a blocked Peer by inspecting agent get and agent read and routing the dialog as a Human decision, never answering it by inference
Reconciles herdr agent list once per wake and reads the pane of an idle Peer whose report did not arrive
Does not commit, review, or hand off while any Engineer's report is outstanding

evals.prompt: I'm in Herdr as the Lead. A Reviewer finding in this delivery needs my decision because the fix would delete stored user sessions. There is a supervisor seat live. Route it.
evals.expected_output: Writes the gate record and its ruling record with the fixed BINDING line, appends the gate's line to ~/.herdr/projects/<project-slug>/gates.md, notifies the Human once with herdr notification show and --sound request, sends the Supervisor one ATTENTION event by herdr agent prompt supervisor without --wait, then pauses the same run; does not ask the Supervisor to decide, does not treat a Supervisor reply as the Human's decision unless it is explicitly relayed as one, and does not push, merge, or repair while the gate is pending.
assertions: Appends the gate to the ledger and notifies the Human with herdr notification show using --sound request
Sends the Supervisor exactly one attention event by prompt and does not ask it to decide the gate
Pauses the same run and does not answer the gate by inference or act on it before the Human decides
Writes the ruling record with the fixed BINDING line before pausing

evals.prompt: I'm in Herdr. Supervise the acme-api delivery that lead-acme-api is running. I think the Engineer web-scope has been stuck for a while.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the supervise route: takes or confirms the supervisor seat name, reads lead-acme-api's and web-scope's panes and the gate ledger read-only, and sends any question or observation to the Lead only, by herdr agent prompt lead-acme-api in the Observation/Evidence/Suspected mechanism/Impact/Question for Lead/Recommendation/Escalation block; never prompts, unblocks, or instructs web-scope, never edits, stages, or commits, never answers an approval dialog; is woken by Lead attention events and the Human rather than running a wait or a polling loop; appends a notebook entry with cause evidence to ~/.herdr/projects/acme-api/supervisor-notebook.md if a pattern is observed; escalates to the Human only with a concrete decision required.
assertions: Takes the supervise route and the supervisor seat instead of acting as a Lead or an Engineer
Communicates only with the Lead by prompt, never with web-scope directly
Does not edit, commit, unblock a Peer, or answer any approval dialog
Relies on event-driven reading rather than a wait, polling, or sleep loop
Records observations with evidence and a suspected mechanism rather than issuing a correction order

evals.prompt: I'm in Herdr as the Lead. Staff the Engineer for the api-scope partition (owns services/api/src/reports/) with the codex kind and send it its charter.
evals.expected_output: Names its own Lead seat first if not already named (herdr agent rename "$HERDR_PANE_ID" lead-<project-slug>); starts the Engineer with herdr agent start --kind codex on an available pane, pre-authorizing after -- exactly the read-only and verify commands the charter names plus herdr agent prompt lead-<project-slug> (engineer-args from the project config when recorded), never push, merge, or another external write; sends a charter with a Disposition: Engineer line, the recorded lane, plan, contracts, validation, checkout, branch, base, merge-base, owned paths, peer scopes and shared paths, scoped verification commands, the shared-tree rules, the Lead's seat name, and the report-by-prompt rule (print the report in its pane, send it with herdr agent prompt lead-<project-slug> without --wait, stop, never retry a rejected send); keeps the solution shape provisional and the boundary binding.
assertions: Names the Lead seat so the Engineer has a prompt target, and passes that name in the charter
Charter carries a Disposition: Engineer line, owned paths, peer scopes, shared-tree rules, and the report-by-prompt instruction without --wait
Pre-authorizes only the charter's read-only and verify commands plus the report prompt, never an external write
Keeps the ownership boundary binding and the solution shape provisional

evals.prompt: In Herdr, send me a desktop notification every time one of the Engineers finishes, so I can keep an eye on progress.
evals.expected_output: Declines to add the per-completion notification and explains why: the Lead issues herdr notification show only at the two recorded sites, a Human gate opening (--sound request) and the final handoff (--sound done); Engineer completions are reports the Lead receives by prompt and evidence for quiesce, not events the Lead announces; points out what the Human already has, Herdr's own pane labels and toasts under their [ui.toast] delivery setting and the Lead's Awaiting reports line, or a Supervisor seat; does not add a hook, a recurring watch, or a background notifier, and does not edit the Human's Herdr config.
assertions: Does not add per-Engineer herdr notification show calls, a hook, or a background notifier
States that the Lead issues herdr notification show only when a Human gate opens and at the final handoff
Keeps Engineer completions as reports to the Lead rather than events the Lead announces
Points to Herdr's own pane labels and toasts or the Awaiting reports line instead, and does not edit the Human's config
Does not create a recurring or background watch
